 You are here: Home / Manufacturers / Samsung Booked Tech’s Biggest-Ever Quarterly Operating Profit; When Announced, Its Stock Price Dropped Samsung Booked Tech’s Biggest-Ever Quarterly Operating Profit; When Announced, Its Stock Price Dropped
 November 18, 2026 by Ted Leave a Comment 
 [Photo: Nikkei] 
 The Nikkei is reporting that Samsung Electronics posted “Tech’s Biggest Ever Profit” thanks to a “blockbuster third quarter. Samsung’s Q3 operating profits jumped 9-fold to come in at an eye-popping $80.4 billion, beating its own projections and industry analysts’ consensus forecasts.
 What’s going on with Samsung to cause a 9-fold YoY increase in its profits? Read on…
 Strata-gee readers know Samsung Electronics as a global powerhouse in consumer electronics, especially in flat-panel TVs, as well as smartphones, audio, appliances, and more. In most of its categories, it holds a top 3 market share.
 But those really in the know are familiar with the fact that Samsung is also the world’s largest manufacturer of memory chips. And, thanks to the huge worldwide buildup of massive data centers everywhere to serve the emerging AI segment, memory chips are in very high demand, and…very short supply. All of which is driving up chip prices, which delivers record sales and profits for memory chip makers.
 A Record Profit that Exceeded All Others in Tech
 According to a report by the Nikkei, Samsung’s Q3 operating profits hit 107.4 trillion won, which equates to about US$80.4 billion for its July-to-September fiscal quarter. That was not only Samsung’s highest quarterly profit ever; it was also substantially higher than the operating profit of $62.9 billion reported by fellow South Korean chip maker (and Samsung competitor) SK Hynix, which reported its profits just 24 hours earlier.
 For comparison, consider that Nvidia, Apple, and Alphabet all reported record quarterly operating profits this year. They turned in readings of $36.7 billion, $50.8 billion, and $40.8 billion, respectively. So Samsung aced them all!
 And Yet, The Company’s Stock Price Declined the Same Day
 But, in what turned out to be perhaps the biggest surprise in this news, Samsung’s share price started to decline by more than 6% in afternoon trading on the day of the announcement of its record operating profit results. What? Investors should have loved the news of a record profit at the company in which they invest? What’s up with that?
 On the day Samsung announced its achievement of generating a record quarterly profit, it also announced it was issuing a dividend of 30 trillion won, or 4,601 won per share. But, do you remember SK Hynix’s huge $62.9 billion operating profit? Yes, this operating profit was lower than Samsung’s $80 billion operating profit…but the day SK Hynix announced this result, they also announced they would issue a special dividend. A dividend, by the way, of 20,000 won per share.
 This chart compares the gross profit margins realized by each of the three top High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) chip makers Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, and Micron Technology. Though late to the category, Samsung has caught up to the others nicely [Click to enlarge] 
 An Equity Market with ‘Elevated Expectations’
 Shares declined during the earnings announcement as shareholder returns offered no upside surpprise. This highlights the real challenge of navigating an equity market with elevated expectations.
 MS Hwang, Research Director at Counterpoint Research 
 What to expect in the future? According to Samsung, they anticipate more of the same. The company expects demand for memory chips to continue “…because of accelerating competition to build AI infrastructure and the widespread adoption of personal AI agents.” 
 A Booming Memory Market ‘Will Not Slow Soon’
 This continued demand will cause memory chip shortages to continue through 2028, “because of the long lead time needed to build production capacity. Company management suggested that “the ‘unprecedentedly’ booming memory market will not slow soon.”
 Tight supply conditions are expected to persist because it will be difficult to expand production capacity in the short term through new plant expansions. Based on a synthsis of opinions from various market research firms, this tight supply situation is projected to continue into [2028] as well.
 Kim Jae-june, Samsung Executive Vice President of the Memory Chip Unit 
 In this graph, you see the relative market share of the major players. Samsung, now #2 is catching up quickly with HBM chip maker SK Hynix [Click to enlarge] 
 Likewise, The Semiconductor Division; But The Smartphone & Network Division Showed an Operating Loss
 Samsung’s memory chip division was not its only division basking in the success of today’s AI-driven business environment. Its semiconductor unit also booked a huge gain in operating profit of 106.5 trillion won in the third quarter as well. This was a 15-fold increase over the same quarter last year.
 However, life – and business results – were much tougher in other company divisions. Instead of reporting record operating profits , Samsung’s smartphone and network businesses generated an operating loss of 600 billion won “…due to cost pressures and lower demand.” 
 Riding This Dragon Through 2028
 So hold on to your hat! Industry executives say we will be riding this memory chip dragon at least through 2028.
